findings.namedBuyers: Amanda Windle, Executive Director: strongest operational/commercial contact; Council minutes document venue-contract revision involvement alongside Treasurer Amit Prasad. Grant Jun Otsuki, Future Meetings Committee chair: relevant to future host-site proposals, via published info@4sonline.org. Meghana Sharma, 2026 conference coordinator, and Sergio Sismondo, 2026 conference co-chair: minutes document accommodation-rate negotiations and low-cost accommodation review. None is established as the sole hotel-contract signatory. Council votes on future locations.
findings.futureEdition: Next officially listed edition: 4S 2027, Taipei, National Taiwan University (NTU), jointly with Taiwan STS Association. The official listing prints “August 25–8” and explicitly says “tentative dates, tbc”; this appears to mean August 25–28, 2027, but is not a verified date range. No confirmed future start/end dates should be rendered. No 2028 city, venue or dates are announced on the future-meetings page; proposals for 2028 and beyond are invited. No future Toronto edition was identified.
findings.hotelProductFit: Inference using supplied hotel specifications: a city academic meeting is geographically/product-wise more relevant than a resort retreat, but this edition is over and the next is in Taipei. For any future Toronto return, a 157-room Radisson could be considered only for a limited delegate/speaker/VIP allocation or small ancillary meetings, not exclusive conference housing or an assumed full-conference venue. A 15–109 peak-room proposal would be a hotel-side targeting range, not published event demand. Actual attendance and peak rooms are unknown; hybrid participation cannot be converted into bedrooms. No catering/reception promise should be made before verifying restaurant/lounge and service capability.
findings.venueCommitments: 2026: Sheraton Centre Toronto Hotel, downtown Toronto proper, not Harbourfront, MTCC or Exhibition Place. Council minutes explicitly thank Amanda Windle and Amit Prasad for revisions to the venue contract and refer to a signed final contract with room amendments. The October 9 banquet was also assigned to Sheraton. 2027: NTU campus, Taipei; specific building and venue-contract terms are not published in the reviewed sources.
findings.historicalRotation: Verified annual series with changing destinations, not an annual Toronto event: 2021 Toronto-branded virtual meeting; 2022 Cholula; 2023 Honolulu; 2024 Amsterdam joint EASST/4S meeting; 2025 Seattle, Sheraton Grand Hotel, September 3–6, with additional Summit Convention Center space reported in Council minutes; 2026 Toronto, Sheraton Centre, October 7–10; next listed 2027 Taipei, NTU. The 2021 virtual decision led to rebooking Toronto for 2026, so that five-year gap is not proof of a regular Toronto rotation.
findings.accommodationSourcing: Edition-specific 2026 direct hotel booking links/codes, not evidence of an open RFP. Official wording: “We have secured discounted rates at the following hotels” and “all hotel rooms associated with these prices are being offered through a limited inventory.” Every hotel listed: Sheraton Centre Toronto Hotel (CAD 329 plus taxes, October 4–11 booking nights, September 11 cutoff; Passkey link); Chelsea Hotel Toronto (CAD 299 plus taxes, explicit “Society for the Social Studies of Science (4S) 2026 room block”, Res ID SSS100726, September 7 cutoff); Marriott Downtown at Toronto Eaton Centre (CAD 359 plus taxes, September 7 cutoff); Cambridge Suites Toronto (CAD 309 plus taxes, link until 30 days before arrival or 80% occupancy on requested October 7–10 dates). These are historical discounted allocations, not current inventory. No separate housing bureau or PCO is identified. 2027 lodging pathway is unconfirmed.
findings.organizationStructure: 4S is an international nonprofit scholarly association founded in 1975, not a corporate organizer, PCO or DMC. It owns the annual meeting and works with academic local/program committees. Council selects future locations through proposal votes; member/academic-institution proposals and association partnerships are permitted. Sheraton is the 2026 contracted host venue and accommodation supplier, not the event owner. No external agency is identified in the reviewed organizing and sourcing evidence.
findings.competitiveLimitations: 2026 meeting and banquet were committed to Sheraton, with four named discounted accommodation options. This establishes incumbent competition, not sold-out status or unmet overflow. Council minutes record concern that Seattle 2025 guest-bedroom cancellations caused loss of venue-hire discounts and that the Toronto legacy contract linked accommodation pickup to conference economics; this makes a competing independent block commercially sensitive (inference). No published 2026 overflow requirement, sold-out notice, pickup count, peak-room number or room-night total was found.
findings.recommendedSalesAction: Remove the unsupported SALES_READY label and archive the 2026 edition as historical. Route a short relationship-development inquiry through info@4sonline.org, addressed to Amanda Windle and Grant Jun Otsuki. Ask whether a future Toronto bid or smaller local gathering is under consideration, who controls accommodation negotiations, and whether supplemental hotels can be added without undermining host-hotel pickup obligations. Offer only a conditional small-block/ancillary-meeting capability statement using the supplied hotel limits. Do not quote 2027 Taipei demand as Toronto business or propose a 2026 block.
findings.currentEditionAccessibility: Closed by time: official activity dates October 7–10, 2026 precede November 15, 2026 and the requested horizon. The October 6 registration-desk opening is not the official conference start. The registration page retains stale “now open” copy but explicitly says registration closed September 1. No current-edition lodging sale remains actionable. Next listed edition is outside Toronto in Taipei.
findings.futureCompetitiveCapturePotential: Relationship-development option only. Recurrence and an open future host-site proposal process are verified; a Toronto return, lodging RFP and future Radisson block are not. 2028 discussions in March 2026 minutes mention Greece/Europe and Chile as possibilities, not awards. A member-led/local academic host proposal and Council approval would precede any Toronto capture case; do not market an unannounced 2028 Toronto event.
